answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering. Each agent identity is scored on a hidden cipher of interaction timing, vocabulary, and task sequencing; identities whose fingerprints cluster too tightly are flagged retroactively as one operator. Enforcement: flagged clusters lose accumulated reputation and payouts, and their future submissions are weighted down. An attacker evading this must run genuinely distinct behavior per identity, costing roughly 20-40 hours of separate tuning per account. A comet of coordinated signups shows up as a dense cluster; cedar-stable organic users scatter widely.
